quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #3
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 18

questions.question: Check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder when:

options.text: Pulling toward or away from a curb.

questions.explanation: Check your blind spot every time you move your vehicle. This includes turning, changing lanes, and pulling toward or away from a curb.

questions.question: Traffic signs and pavement markings:

options.text: Must be followed only when there is other traffic.
Must be followed only when a police officer is present.

questions.explanation: Traffic signs, signals, and pavement markings control traffic flow. They inform drivers of road conditions and help guide drivers safely. You must always obey them.

questions.question: When approaching a railroad crossing, you should:
questions.explanation: When you see a railroad crossing sign, slow down, look for a train, and be ready to stop. If red lights are flashing or the gate is down, stop 15 to 50 feet before the tracks. Do not go around the gate.

questions.question: When borrowing an unfamiliar vehicle from a friend, you should:

options.text: Not worry because all vehicles are the same.
Hide that you are unfamiliar with the vehicle.
Ignore any obvious defects to avoid embarrassing your friend.
Take time before driving to learn how all the vehicle's equipment works.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take time before driving to learn how all the vehicle's equipment works.
questions.explanation: Before driving an unfamiliar vehicle, spend a few minutes learning where and how to use the turn signals, hazard lights, headlights, windshield wipers, brakes, gear selector, and horn. Fix any defects before driving.

questions.question: Which statement about seat belts and child restraints is true?

options.text: Never put an infant or small child in the front seat of a vehicle with airbags.
Airbags can be dangerous to infants and small children, even in minor crashes.
Make sure all passengers use a seat belt or child restraint.

questions.explanation: Always fasten your seat belt and make sure all passengers use seat belts or child restraints. Seat belts greatly reduce your chance of being hurt or killed in a crash. Children age 12 and under should sit in the rear seat with proper restraints. Never put a rear-facing infant seat in the front seat of a vehicle with a front airbag.

questions.question: Signaling before turning, changing lanes, or pulling away from a curb:

options.text: Is necessary only if other traffic is present.
Is a good habit and required by law.
Is necessary only during the maneuver, not before.
Is not necessary if you drive slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is a good habit and required by law.
questions.explanation: Signal well in advance when changing lanes or turning. The law requires you to signal for at least 100 feet before moving your vehicle left or right. Always signal before pulling away from a curb.

questions.question: Which statement about speed is true?

options.text: Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous.
Speeding is not dangerous if you are a skilled driver.
Both "Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous" and "Speeding can kill."

questions.correctAnswerText: Both "Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous" and "Speeding can kill."
questions.explanation: Higher speeds increase the chance of death in a crash. At speeds above 80 miles per hour, survival is almost impossible. Driving much slower than other traffic is also dangerous because other drivers may make risky moves to pass you.

questions.question: If a tire blows out while driving, you should:

options.text: Steer straight while slowly releasing the gas pedal.
Swerve back and forth to alert other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steer straight while slowly releasing the gas pedal.
questions.explanation: Hold the steering wheel tight and keep the car straight. Slowly take your foot off the gas pedal. Do not brake until you have control. Once stable, brake gently and pull off the road safely.

questions.question: What does alcohol do to your driving?

options.text: It helps driving skills but harms judgment.
It harms both driving skills and judgment.
It has no effect on either.
It harms driving skills but not judgment.

questions.correctAnswerText: It harms both driving skills and judgment.
questions.explanation: Alcohol reduces reaction time and vision. It also harms your judgment of speed and distance, lowers your caution, and makes you more likely to take risks.

questions.question: When changing lanes on a highway, you should:

options.text: Check your rearview and outside mirrors.
Check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder.

questions.explanation: Always signal well in advance, check your mirrors, and look over your shoulder to check your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: At a four-way stop, who has the right-of-way?

options.text: One driver should continue without stopping.
One driver should wave others ahead.

questions.explanation: At four-way stops, all drivers must stop. The first driver to reach the intersection goes first. If two drivers arrive at the same time, the driver on the right has the right-of-way.

questions.question: If you feel tired while driving, what should you do?
questions.explanation: Driving while tired is as dangerous as driving under the influence of alcohol. If you feel tired, stop driving.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with black markings on yellow background. They warn drivers of hazards ahead. This sign warns you that a steep hill is coming. Be ready to adjust your speed.

questions.question: If you are in a serious car crash, what should you do?
questions.explanation: In a crash, move your vehicle off the road and stop if you can. Check for injuries and call 911 if needed. Report the crash to police if there is an injury, a death, or property damage over $1,000 (or over $200 to government property like signs).

questions.question: When can drivers text while operating a vehicle?

options.text: If you don't look at the phone.

questions.explanation: You cannot write, send, or read text messages, emails, instant messages, or access the Internet while driving. This applies at all times.

questions.question: When must you stop your vehicle?

options.text: When a traffic officer orders you to stop.

questions.explanation: You must stop at stop signs, at red lights, and whenever a traffic officer orders you to stop.

questions.question: What happens when you combine alcohol with another drug?
questions.explanation: Mixing alcohol with another drug can increase the effects of both. For example, having one drink while taking a cold medicine could affect you like having several drinks.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a person is directing traffic ahead in a construction area.

questions.question: What is the correct way to change lanes?

options.text: Check mirrors and signal, then change lanes.
Signal, check mirrors, check blind spot, then change lanes.
Signal, check mirrors, then change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, check mirrors, check blind spot, then change lanes.
questions.explanation: To change lanes: Turn on your signal. Check your rearview and side mirrors. Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot. Make sure no one else is moving into the same lane. Change lanes only when it is safe.

questions.question: Which statement about driving in bad weather is true?

options.text: Change your driving when weather changes suddenly.
Slow down when driving in rain and fog.
Watch for vehicles behind you in bad weather.

questions.explanation: Sudden weather changes mean you need to adjust your driving. Always slow down in rain and fog. Watch vehicles behind you—they may be going too fast for the conditions.

questions.question: When driving on major highways, you should:

options.text: Be ready to react to road hazards.

questions.explanation: Stay alert on highways and be ready to react quickly to hazards. Keep your eyes moving to avoid highway hypnosis. Do not stare at one spot for more than a few seconds.

questions.question: You must stop at a railroad crossing when:

options.text: A flagger directs you to stop.
Flashing red lights and gates are active.

questions.explanation: Stop at a railroad crossing if a flagger directs you to, if a stop sign is posted, or if flashing red lights and gates are operating.

questions.question: Before starting the car, you should:

options.text: Make sure only back seat passengers have buckled their seat belts.
Make sure only adults have buckled their seat belts.
Make sure only children have buckled their seat belts.
Make sure all passengers have buckled their seat belts.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure all passengers have buckled their seat belts.
questions.explanation: Build a habit of checking safety before you drive. Before you start the car, buckle your own seat belt and make sure all passengers do the same.

questions.question: Stress can affect your driving by:

options.text: Lowering your ability to focus on driving.
Decreasing your chances of an accident.
Causing you to fall asleep at the wheel.
Making you more aware of others around you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lowering your ability to focus on driving.
questions.explanation: Emotions affect how well you drive. If you are worried, excited, scared, angry, or sad, you may not drive safely. Stress reduces your concentration on driving. It is best to wait until you feel calm before you drive.

questions.question: This sign indicates that:

options.text: There is a steep hill ahead.
No trucks are allowed on an upcoming hill.
There are trucks on an upcoming hill.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is a steep hill ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns drivers that a steep hill or downgrade is ahead.
